messages:
sam_sales: Hey team — customer (FinServCo) POC question. They have an MPLS-connected on-prem datacenter and force all egress through a corporate forward proxy. They want Private deployment in our VPC but need to know: can Redwood Private work behind their proxy? Is PrivateLink or VPC peering better given they won't accept inbound peering from our side? Also need exact firewall/egress IPs and ports (and any SNI or TLS fingerprinting) for the POC.

lina_se: Short answer: PrivateLink is usually better when customers only allow inbound PrivateLink endpoints or don't want routing changes. But with a forced web proxy for egress, we need to confirm client-initiated connections from the customer's side can reach our Private control plane. Do they expect outbound calls to our control plane or do they prefer an air-gapped agent?

ellen_it: They can't open new inbound routes; all connections must be outbound via proxy. They can allow TCP/443 to specific FQDNs and IP ranges. They also require mTLS for control-plane calls.

raj_network: For PrivateLink we usually create an interface endpoint in their VPC — that requires a cross-account endpoint service. If they disallow peering and only allow outbound via proxy, PrivateLink won't work unless their proxy can resolve and proxy traffic to the ENIs in the VPC. Alternative: leverage our Private deployment with a customer-managed NAT/proxy in their VPC that forwards to our control plane via TLS with client certs. Key point: we can accept outbound connections from customer to our control plane on 443 with mutual TLS.

mira_security: We support mTLS for control-plane auth for Private customers (cert provisioning via CA). For the POC we can provide temporary client cert + CA bundle. We'll need the customer's allowed IP ranges for auditing but we don't require a fixed source IP for session-hosted workloads (if they use PrivateLink ENIs we will provide IPs).

lina_se: Network checklist I can provide: 1) Outbound 443 to control plane FQDNs (we'll list), 2) DNS resolution for our service names (CNAME to redwood-priv-...accounts), 3) If using PrivateLink, allow connections to the interface ENI IPs we create, 4) If using VPC peering/TGW, add routes to our service prefixes, 5) If corporate forward proxy is used, confirm SNI passthrough and that it allows forwarding to our endpoints, 6) mTLS cert install process.

sam_sales: Ellen — can you share whether the proxy allows SNI passthrough and client certs? That will determine approach.

ellen_it: Proxy vendor is BlueProxy v6 — supports SNI passthrough but strips client certs by default. There is an appliance mode that preserves mTLS if we use a direct NAT instead.

raj_network: If client certs are stripped, PrivateLink with our interface endpoints won't get the certs unless the proxy is in passthrough mode. So likely convo: either they enable passthrough, or they run a small bastion NAT that preserves TLS to our control plane.

onboarding_pm: I'll draft the POC steps and the minimal firewall whitelist. Sam — can you confirm if we need any additional ports for metrics, agent heartbeats, or S3 offloads?

lina_se: For POC minimal: outbound 443 (HTTPS) to control plane FQDNs, outbound 443 to model artifact S3 endpoints (we can use presigned URLs to avoid IP allowlist), DNS to resolve our service zone, and optionally allow inbound to an interface ENI if they pick PrivateLink. No other ports required. We'll send the exact FQDN/IP list.

sam_sales: Thanks — Mira can you generate a temporary cert + list of service FQDNs and the enforcement notes? Also need pricing note: customer asked if Dedicated reserved capacity adds any different network requirements vs Private.

mira_security: Certs: yes we can spin temporary mTLS certs for the POC. Pricing: Dedicated capacity is still hosted inside our VPC and uses same control plane endpoints; network whitelist is identical. Dedicated only changes capacity SLA and data isolation, not port lists.

deploy-bot: deploy notice: created ticket INF-7892 to track POC network changes and cert issues.

sam_sales: Great. I'll loop in customer and propose two options: 1) enable proxy passthrough for mTLS + PrivateLink, or 2) deploy small NAT/proxy in their VPC to preserve TLS and use outbound-only connections. Thanks folks :thumbsup:
